text:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty — incident triggered: Service=\`inference-serving\`, Incident #54321, Priority=P1. Reason: 5xx-rate above 5% (3m), p95 latency >1200ms. Escalation policy: oncall -> secondary -> manager. :rotating_light:

incident-bot: Alert snapshot:
- 5xx-rate: 6.8% (3m)
- p95 latency: 1.35s
- error family: upstream 502s and model worker OOMs
- affected route: /v1/generate (hosted)

alice: ack (oncall) — grabbing laptop, joining thread.

pagerduty-bot: No ack from primary within 90s. Escalating to secondary (bob).

bob: ack — I see the alert. pinging alice on voice. starting triage.

alice: sorry, was on mobile and didn’t see the push. on laptop now. copying logs.

dave: quick note — we’ve seen a pattern where one of the model-pool nodes (worker-3) did an oom and restarted; rolling errors after that.

emma: Support: customer-impact flags show ~12 customers experiencing >30% error rate on gen requests, a handful on paid Dedicated clusters reported increased latency. Notified CS.

bob: first step — check pod status and recent restarts.

infra-bot: Command executed: ```kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector=app=inference-runtime
NAME                          READY  STATUS   RESTARTS   AGE
inference-runtime-0           2/2    Running  0          3d
inference-runtime-1           2/2    Running  1          3d
inference-runtime-2           2/2    Running  0          3d
inference-runtime-3           0/2    CrashLoopBackOff  6  2h
```

alice: worker-3 CrashLoopBackOff with OOM. I’ll pull the last stderr.

infra-bot: Logs (tail): ```[2026-03-15T02:14:21Z] gpu0: allocate() failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T02:14:22Z] model: allocate kv cache failed, fallback triggered
[2026-03-15T02:14:24Z] runtime: fatal: oom, exit code 137
```

bob: ok — it’s a real OOM. Could be bimodal spike in sequence length or bad caching. Mitigation options: a) restart the bad pod b) scale up pool c) route traffic to smaller quantized variant (redwood-llama-7b-q4) d) temporary autoscaling override. Thoughts?

carol: paging me as manager because secondary acked during escalation. How long for containment estimate?

alice: immediate action: drain worker-3, restart pod, and add one extra replica to absorb load. If OOM recurs, flip traffic to smaller model.

bob: executing containment: ```kubectl cordon pod/inference-runtime-3 -n inference || true
kubectl delete pod inference-runtime-3 -n inference --grace-period=10 --force
kubectl scale deployment/inference-runtime -n inference --replicas=5```

infra-bot: Scale command accepted — replicas -> 5. Restart initiated.

pagerduty-bot: Secondary acknowledged (bob). Manager paged (carol) — acknowledgement pending.

carol: ack — on the bridge. good catch. want to confirm rollback window for latest model build?

alice: last deploy was a micro-ops change to KV cache tuning 2h ago. No full model change. I’ll run a quick config diff.

dave: I’m watching CPU/GPU heatmaps and network egress. No unusual network saturation. GPU memory pressure is elevated on worker-2 too. Recommendation: temporarily route x% of traffic to smaller model to reduce memory pressure while we stabilize.

bob: implementing traffic split via router config: ``routerctl route set /v1/generate --weight redwood-llama-7b-q4=30 --weight redwood-llama-13b=70`` — applying now.

infra-bot: Router updated. 30% traffic to redwood-llama-7b-q4.

alice: monitoring error rates and p95 after split.

incident-bot: After mitigation snapshot (2m): 5xx-rate -> 1.2%, p95 -> 920ms. Partial containment success. :thumbsup:

emma: Notifying top-affected customers: sent initial status email and ETA for update. Logging incident tags for billing/regression tracking.

carol: thanks team. not elevating to SEV1 customer-wide outage. We should keep page open until stable for 15m. Please collect incident timeline.

bob: assigning postmortem: owners=alice + dave. reminder to include root cause hypothesis (OOM due to mem pressure + KV cache growth) and mitigation (autoscale thresholds, fallback route automation).

alice: capture config diffs and container memory limits. I’ll open a PR for a guardrail to failover to q4 model when p95>1s and 5xx>3% for 2m.

dave: also suggest adding a watch to auto-scale GPU pool when average gpu_mem_util > 85% for 3m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident #54321 acknowledged by bob and carol. Incident set to status=acknowledged.

incident-bot: Closing notes: containment achieved via pod restart + scale + model split. Customer impact limited to transient errors for ~12 customers. Follow-up items: postmortem, automated fallback, autoscale rule.

alice: thanks everyone. will schedule postmortem and link here when drafted. :white_check_mark:
